d: Type requiring concrete implementations; cannot be instantiated directly.
Same name denotes different implementations for different argument types (overloading).
Type formed by sum (union) and product (record) of other types.
The classic Hindley-Milner type_inference algorithm combining constraint_generation, most_general_unifier computation, and let-polymorphism generalization in a single pass producing principal_type.
Lifted function application over wrapped values enabling multi-argument composition.
Homogeneous mutable sequence with element type (list[int] in Python).
Asynchronous computation that may succeed with value or fail with error.
Type representing asynchronous computation (Future[T], Promise<T>, Task<T>).
Automatic implicit boxing/unboxing between primitives and their wrapper types.

A mode of type_inference splitting into two directions: synthesize (produce a type from an expression alone) and check (verify an expression against a given expected_type), composed via type_environment.
Temporary access to data without taking ownership, with borrow checker enforcement.
Type with no values (never in TypeScript, Nothing in Scala) — uninhabited.
Wrapping primitive value in heap-allocated object wrapper (int → Integer).
Fluent API constructing complex objects step-by-step with method chaining and type-safe setters.
Explicit programmer assertion to interpret value as different type (unsafe in many langs).
Object blueprint combining data fields, methods, and potentially inheritance.
Automatic generation of type-safe code from type definitions or schemas.
Generic container type (List[T], Set[T], Map[K,V]) with element type parameter.
Type system accepts every valid program (relative to its formal semantics).
Type constructed from other types (tuple, array, object, function).
Type-level conditional selecting between two types based on condition (T extends U ? X : Y).
An atomic equational condition of the form type_A = type_B produced during constraint_generation, awaiting resolution by unification.
The phase that walks the syntax tree of an expression under a type_environment, producing a set of constraints paired with an accumulating type_environment for subterms.
Set of type equality constraints generated during constraint-based type inference.
The phase that processes the generated constraints via unification, producing the principal substitution.
Generic reverses subtyping direction for input positions (Consumer[-A]).
Generic preserves subtyping direction for output positions (Producer[+A]).
A type variable bound by a ∀ quantifier in a type scheme; subject to instantiation.
A type equality constraint τ₁ ~ τ₂ arising during inference; must be unified to complete typing.
A program expression undergoing type inference; the subject of a typing judgment.
A type variable free in a type (not bound by a surrounding type scheme); scoped via the type environment.
A type variable generated during instantiation or constraint solving; distinct from all existing variables.
The operation that abstracts free type variables in a monotype to form a type scheme when binding a let-expression.
The operation that replaces quantified variables in a type scheme with fresh type variables to obtain a monotype.
Most General Unifier; the unique (up to renaming) substitution that is more general than any other unifier of the same constraints.
The property of a type being maximal under the instance relation; no other valid type is more general.
Most general type that captures all valid typings for an expression; all other valid types are instances of it via substitution.
A type substitution mapping type variables to types; the mechanism that relates principal type to its instances.
A type; the target of typing judgments; can be monomorphic or polymorphic.
The context Γ mapping term variables to their types or type schemes during inference.
A polymorphic type (polytype) of the form ∀α₁...αₙ. τ expressing that τ may be instantiated by replacing the quantified variables.
A flexible type variable appearing in an inferred type; subject to unification and occurs-check.
A judgment of the form Γ ⊢ e : τ asserting expression e has type τ under type environment Γ.
The algorithm that computes the most general unifier of a set of type constraints; yields a substitution.
Isomorphism between types and logical propositions, programs and proofs.
Wrapping objects to add behavior at runtime without altering the wrapped type.
Pair where second component type depends on first component value.
Type that depends on a runtime value, enabling compile-time proofs about data.
Reconstructing typed objects from serialized representation with type safety concerns.
Key-value mapping type (dict[K,V] in Python, Map<K,V> in Java).
Tagged union enabling compiler-verified exhaustive pattern matching over variants.
A discriminated union with exactly two du_variant cases. Historically called 'Either' or sum-of-two; many algebraic laws simplify for the binary case.
A discriminated union whose variant set is fixed and final; no new variants can be introduced. Common in languages with sealed hierarchies or final sum types.
The static guarantee that a du_match covers every du_variant of the discriminated union. The type system rejects non-exhaustive matches, ensuring no variant is silently ignored.
The introduction form for a discriminated union: given a variant label and a payload of the matching type, produce a value of the union type. Also called 'variant' or 'Left'/'Right' in binary cases.
The elimination form: a function that, given a discriminated union value, dispatches on its du_tag to apply the appropriate handler to the du_payload, yielding a uniform result type.
A discriminated union where each du_variant is identified by a distinct type name (nominal typing). The du_tag is implicit in the variant's name; runtime representation may be optimized away.
A discriminated union that permits new variants to be added in extension modules or subtypes without breaking existing du_match arms. Contrast with du_closed.
The data value carried by a specific variant of a discriminated union. Only one payload is live at a time; the tag selects which one.
An untagged union of types without a du_tag. The discriminated union adds a tag to this primitive structure to make variant membership verifiable.
A discriminated union where variants are distinguished by their shape (payload type) rather than by name. The du_tag must be stored at runtime to disambiguate structurally identical variants.
A value-level or type-level label that uniquely identifies which variant of a discriminated union is active in a given value. The tag is the first-class evidence of variant membership.
A named constituent of a discriminated union, pairing a du_tag with a du_payload type. Each variant represents one summand in the sum type.
Typing based on object capabilities rather than declared type or inheritance.
Type checking performed at runtime during execution.
Type-level tracking of side effects (IO, state, exceptions) beyond return type.
Fixed finite set of named constant values (enum in Python/Rust/TypeScript).
Type representing failure conditions as values rather than exceptions.
Union of value type and error type representing failure as ordinary value.
Guarantee about object and resource state when exceptions propagate.
Compiler verification that all cases of a union are handled in pattern matching.
Abstraction hiding a type (some T such that property holds) from consumers.
Existential quantifier over types meaning some hidden type T satisfies property.
Constructor abstraction returning possibly-different subtypes based on input parameters.
Type or class that cannot be extended or subclassed (final in Java/Kotlin).
Universal quantifier over types meaning property holds for all types T.
Set of type variables occurring in a type that are not quantified; relevant to generalization.
Callable type specifying parameter types and return type (x: Callable[[int], str]).
Mappable wrapper where map applies function to contained value preserving structure.
Operation that abstracts free type variables into quantified variables, forming a type scheme.
Lazy sequence producing values via coroutine-like suspension (yield).
Bound restricting type variable to subset of types (T extends Comparable in Java).
Type or function parameterized by one or more type variables enabling code reuse across types.
Removing static annotations preserves runtime behavior; adding them never breaks it.
Mixing statically-typed and dynamically-typed code with consistency checks at boundary.
Type constructor taking another type as argument (Functor[F[_]] in Scala).
Classical type inference algorithm supporting parametric polymorphism and let-generalization.
Polymorphism allowing polymorphic types inside other types (System F — e.g. Java generics).
Operation that replaces quantified variables in a type scheme with fresh type variables.
Contract specifying required fields and/or methods without implementation details.
Value must satisfy all constituent types simultaneously (A & B).
Generic has no subtyping relationship regardless of component types (mutable container).
A bidirectional optic between two types that are isomorphic, providing both a forward view and a reverse constructor with no information loss.
Lazy traversal abstraction yielding elements one at a time on demand.
Type of a type — arity classification (* is proper type, *→* is type constructor).
Types implied by operations rather than declared; checked at use site.
A pure projection from a product type to a specific du_payload at a named field, extracting only the target substructure without mutation.
An optic pairing a getter with a setter over a product type's field, enabling focused access to one du_payload while preserving the rest of the product structure.
A mutation function taking a product type and a new du_payload value, returning a new product with only the target field replaced, leaving all other du_payload fields unchanged.
Composable accessor/mutator pair for nested immutable data structures.
The scoping discipline that generalizes the rhs of a let-binding at its point of definition, making its type_scheme available for instantiation at each use site.
Region of code during which a reference remains valid (Rust lifetime annotations).
Refinement types with automatically inferred predicates using SMT solving.
Requiring explicit type declarations for all bindings (Java, C++).
Type transforming each member of another type (Record<K,V> in TypeScript).
Guarantee preventing invalid memory access: buffer overflows, use-after-free, dangling pointers.
Composable behavior units mixed into classes via inheritance or composition.
Type wrapper with bind operation chaining computations with context (Result, Option).
Type with no quantified variables; ground type or type variable instantiation result.
Property of a type such that no strictly more general type exists for the same expression.
Most general substitution that satisfies a set of type constraints; unique up to renaming of variables.
Set of types referencing each other forming a cycle (AST node variants).
Static type checker for Python implementing PEP 484 type annotations.
Type refinement in conditional branches reducing possible types (v: int | str → v: int).
Type wrapper distinguishing semantically different values of same representation.
Subtyping relationship declared explicitly via class/interface inheritance.
Type compatibility determined by explicit declaration and name identity.
Reference pointing to absent object causing crash on dereference if unchecked.
Type system preventing null dereference by distinguishing nullable from non-null types.
Structured data bundling named fields and methods; blueprint for runtime instances.
The guard inside unification that rejects a substitution {α ↦ t} when α occurs free inside t, preventing the construction of infinite recursive types.
Type whose internal structure is hidden from consumers (abstract type with hidden representation).
Composition rule: chaining optics so the du_payload of one becomes the structure operated on by the next, forming a pipeline that satisfies the optic laws transitively.
Law: applying lens_setter to the result of lens_getter on any product yields back the original du_payload value — get never lies about what set just wrote.
Law: applying lens_getter to the result of lens_setter on a product yields back the du_payload value that was set — set reflects exactly what get will retrieve.
Law: composing two lens_setter calls yields the same product as applying only the second one — idempotent in the face of duplicate mutation, last du_payload wins.
Law: the composition of a lens_setter with a lens_getter in reverse order yields a total transformation equivalent to the identity on du_payload — structural integrity preserved under round-trip.

Classification of an optic by its directional capability: getter-only (covariant, read-only), setter-only (contravariant, write-only), or full optic (both directions, lenses are the canonical full case).
Abstracting getters/setters across product and sum types (lens, prism, traversal).
Explicit optional value type forcing handling of absence (Option[T], Maybe[T]).
Value may be present (Some/T) or absent (None/Null) — nullable wrapper.
Linear resource management where exactly one owner is responsible for deallocation.
Same implementation works uniformly over a range of types via type parameters.
Type variable appearing only in output positions carrying compile-time metadata.
Recursive function where type argument differs between recursive calls.
Synonym for type scheme; a type with forall-quantified variables enabling polymorphism.
Polymorphism restricted to monomorphic types inside quantifiers (ML/Hindley-Milner).
Built-in atomic types (int, float, bool, str) not composed from other types.

An untagged union of types representing a value that could be one of several member types, but without a discriminator tag or label to identify which variant is active at runtime. Membership cannot be compiler-verified and exhaustive pattern matching is not enforced.
Pair consisting of a type scheme and its originating type environment; the full inference result.
Most general type capturing all valid typings for an expression.
A constructor taking a du_payload and injecting it as the sole du_variant under a specific du_tag, rebuilding the sum type from the selected summand.
A partial function over a sum type that succeeds only when the active du_tag matches the target, yielding the contained du_payload; otherwise the sum is preserved.
An optic pairing a matcher with a builder over a sum type's du_variant, enabling partial projection into one du_tag's du_payload with fallback to the original sum.
Structural type defining required methods without implementation (Swift protocol, Go interface).
The substitution-composition step that replaces a type_variable with its expanded form after unification, eliminating aliasing to type_variables.
principal_type: the unique most-general type that captures all valid typings for an expression, serving as the output of type inference
type_inference: the algorithmic process of deriving types for expressions by propagating constraints from known types through the syntax tree
type_variable: a placeholder symbol in a type that remains unresolved until unification binds it to a concrete or more general type
unification: the algorithm that finds the most general substitution making two types equal, central to constraint solving in inference
substitution: a mapping from type variables to types that, when applied, resolves all variables in a type expression
type_constraint: an equation of the form T1 = T2 between two types that must hold for a valid typing
type_scheme: a type paired with quantified type variables, enabling polymorphism by separating generic from monomorphic occurrences
generalization: the operation that lifts free type variables into a type scheme, forming a polytype from a monotype
instantiation: replacing quantified variables in a type scheme with fresh type variables, yielding a less-general type
most_general_unifier: the substitution produced by unification that is no more restrictive than any other unifier for the same types
let_polymorphism: the polymorphism arising from let-bindings where the bound expression is generalized, giving it a principal type scheme
type_equivalence_class: the set of all types reachable from a principal type via instantiation—types that are all valid typings of the same expression
free_type_variables: type variables occurring in an expression that are not bound by a surrounding lambda and thus subject to generalization
principal_type_theorem: the formal result guaranteeing that when a principal type exists, it is unique up to renaming of type variables
Function producing same output for same input with no side effects.
Fast TypeScript-style type checker for Python using language server protocol.
Fixed set of named fields with individual types (struct in Rust, type alias in TypeScript).
Type containing itself as component (linked list node: value + next node).
Expression replaceable by its value without changing program behavior.
Base type restricted by a predicate (x: {v: int | v > 0}).
Type information preserved and accessible at runtime via reflection or generics reification.
The fresh-variable generation step that replaces a type_variable with a distinct new type_variable during instantiation or when lifting quantifiers, ensuring no capture of free variables.
Failure to release acquired resources causing gradual exhaustion (file handles, memory).
Wrapper capturing either successful value or error without exceptions (Result<T, E>).
Polymorphism over record shapes allowing extension while preserving existing fields.
Validating values against types at runtime (pydantic, attrs, marshmallow).
Verifying data structure conforms to schema (JSON Schema, OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL).
Class limited to known subtypes enabling compiler-verified exhaustive matching.
Transforming in-memory objects to transmittable/recordable format preserving type information.
Collection of unique values with O(1) membership testing (set[T], HashSet<T>).
Observable state change beyond returning a value (I/O, mutation, throwing).
Replacing type variable with fresh unknown type during type inference.
Type system property: well-typed programs cannot go wrong (Milner).
Type checking performed at compile-time before execution.
Encapsulating swappable algorithms behind common interface for runtime selection.
Compiler flag enforcing non-nullability preventing null assignment to non-nullable types.
Language enforcement preventing implicit conversions between unrelated types.
Subtyping relationship inferred from having all required members of supertype.
Type compatibility determined by shape of data (fields present) not by name.
A total function from type_variable to monotype; a mapping recording how each type_variable was solved during constraint_solving.
Code operates on values of a type and all its subtypes via inheritance hierarchy.
Partial ordering between types where subtype values can substitute supertype values.
Parent type higher in a type hierarchy; all subtypes are compatible with it.
Discriminated union with explicit tag field enabling exhaustive pattern matching.
Type computed from string literal allowing string manipulation at type level.
Correct behavior of types and operations under concurrent access from multiple threads.
Supertype of all types (Any in Python/TypeScript, Object in Java) accepting any value.
Operation over a traversal_optic that reduces all targeted du_payload within a structure to a single aggregate value, consuming the structure without producing a new one.
Operation over a traversal_optic that applies a function to each du_payload in the targeted locations, producing a new structure with all positions updated.
An optic generalizing lens and prism to target zero or more locations simultaneously, enabling fold and map operations over collections of du_payload within a structure.
Fixed-length heterogeneous sequence with positional typing (x: tuple[int, str]).
Fundamental classification of values determining permissible operations and memory layout.
Named shorthand for a complex type expression improving readability.
Explicit syntactic marker associating a name or expression with a type (e.g. x: int).
Type hints file (.pyi) providing types without implementation for external libraries.
Concrete type substituted for type parameter at instantiation site.
Static analysis tool verifying type constraints without executing the program.
Process of verifying that program expressions respect declared or inferred type constraints.
Implicit automatic conversion from one type to another (e.g. int to float).
Whether a value of one type may be assigned to a variable of another type.
Type with certain members excluded (TypeScript: string & {} excluding never).
A finite mapping from term_variable names to type_schemes, providing the typing assumptions available at a given point during constraint_generation.
Two types are exactly identical in structure and name (nominal or structural).
Type information discarded during compilation (Java generics pre-14 reification).
Violation of type constraints detected by the type system (static or runtime).
Unwrapping type from container (Option[T] → T via unwrap or pattern match).
Type-level function mapping input types to output types (associated types in Rust traits).
Function narrowing union type to one branch based on runtime check (isinstance).
Compiler or runtime deducing types from context without explicit annotation.
Most specific common supertype of two types (greatest lower bound).
Restricting which types may extend or implement a given type.
Systematic naming rules for types (PascalCase for classes, snake_case for Python).
Compiler inference of more specific type within control flow branch.
Named placeholder within generic declaration awaiting concrete type argument.
Accessing field or method of existential type while hiding the concrete type.
Implicit widening conversion along a type hierarchy (e.g. byte to int).
Builder preventing invalid intermediate states via phantom types encoding construction phase.
Tagged union with exhaustiveness guarantee preventing access without matching on tag.
Property that a program cannot perform invalid operations on values of incorrect type.
Type with universally quantified variables; pairs a monotype with a set of type variables in scope.
Mapping from type variables to types; a function applied to types to resolve variables.
Formal mathematical framework for studying types and their properties.
Least upper bound of two types — value belonging to either type.
Placeholder symbol ranging over types, awaiting instantiation (alpha in Hindley-Milner).
Implicit conversion from narrow subtype to broader supertype.
Centralized repository of standard library type stubs for Python type checkers.
Extracting primitive value from its object wrapper.
The algorithm that, given two monotypes, computes a substitution that makes them syntactically identical, or reports a type_error if impossible.
Value may be one of several alternative types (x: int | str in TypeScript).
Property that any two principal types for the same expression differ only by renaming of type variables.
Abstraction over all types (for all T, property holds) — parametric polymorphism.
A type that can be assigned to an expression under some type environment and substitution.
Rules governing how subtyping relationships between type arguments affect parameterized types.
Explicit (+/-/*) markers on type parameters declaring covariance/contravariance/invariance.
Separating algorithm from object structure using accept/visit dispatch on typed data.
Permissive type system allowing implicit conversions and pointer coercion.
